items.stem: A method is marked async and returns Task<int> but contains no await. What does the compiler do and what happens at run time?

options.text: It warns, and the method runs synchronously
options.rationale: Correct: per the C# model, an async method with no await runs synchronously and the compiler issues a warning.

options.text: It errors and will not compile
options.rationale: The absence of await is a warning, not a compile error.

options.text: It runs on a new thread automatically
options.rationale: async does not by itself move work to another thread.
The method returns normally; it simply does not suspend.

items.explanation: Correct: per the C# model, an async method with no await runs synchronously and the compiler issues a warning.

items.stem: Which TWO statements about value vs reference types in C# are correct? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Assigning a struct copies its value
options.rationale: Correct: structs are value types and are copied on assignment.

options.text: Assigning a class reference copies the reference, not the object
options.rationale: Correct: two references then point to the same object.

options.text: Copying a class instance always deep-copies its fields
options.rationale: Copying a reference does not duplicate the object.

items.explanation: Correct: structs are value types and are copied on assignment.

items.stem: Which numeric type is the appropriate default for storing a currency amount in C#?

options.rationale: Correct: decimal avoids binary floating-point rounding errors for money.
double is binary floating-point and introduces rounding errors for currency.
float has even less precision than double for monetary values.
int cannot represent fractional currency amounts.

items.explanation: Correct: decimal avoids binary floating-point rounding errors for money.
